title: A Day in Taipei
summary: In one day as a tourist in Taipei, you ride the MRT with an EasyCard, order breakfast and bubble tea, go up Taipei 101 and eat at Raohe Night Market.

blocks.title: Introduction
paragraphs: Today we will learn to be tourists for one day. We will learn to take trains, order food, and visit places. We will also practise three conversations.

items.prompt: Have you ever been to Taiwan, or would you like to go?
What do you usually eat for breakfast?

blocks.title: Part 1: From the Airport to the City
paragraphs: Your plane lands at Taoyuan International Airport, near Taipei. The easiest way into the city is the Airport MRT. MRT is the city's train system, like a subway. **The express train takes about 35 minutes to Taipei Main Station. One ride costs NT$160 (New Taiwan dollars).**

Before you get on the train, buy an EasyCard. **An EasyCard is a travel card. You put money on it. Then you touch it on the ticket gate.** It works on the MRT, on the bus and in many shops. In Japan, Suica works the same way.

**The card costs NT$100, but this money is only for the card.** A new card has no money for rides. So you add money at the same time. This is called *topping up*. You can buy a card and top it up in these places.

- 7-Eleven and FamilyMart shops in the airport
- the information desk at the Airport MRT station
- the information desk in any MRT station
**In Taipei, one MRT ride costs NT$20 to NT$65. The price depends on how far you go.**

**One MRT rule surprises many visitors. Past the yellow line in front of the ticket gates, you cannot eat or drink.** No food, no drinks, not even water. The rule is also for the trains and the waiting areas.
Why is the rule so strict? With no food, trains and stations stay clean. **If you break the rule, the fine is NT$1,500 to NT$7,500.** So finish your coffee before you cross the yellow line.

images.alt: A traveller touching a blue EasyCard on a ticket gate at an Airport MRT station, with a train waiting at the platform

blocks.title: Part 2: Breakfast and Bubble Tea
paragraphs: Now you are in the city, and you are hungry. **Many people in Taiwan do not make breakfast at home. They buy it at a small breakfast shop.** These shops open very early. The food is fast and cheap. So people eat it on the way to work or school.
Try these two favourites.

- **dan bing**: a thin, flat bread cooked with an egg. It is rolled up and cut into pieces. It often has cheese, ham or corn in it.
- **soy milk**: a drink made from beans. You can have it hot or cold, sweet or not sweet.
**A simple breakfast like this costs about NT$60 to NT$120.**
After breakfast, it is time for a drink. **Bubble tea comes from Taiwan**, and there is a tea shop on almost every street.
The most famous drink is **pearl milk tea**. It is milk tea with soft balls at the bottom. People call them pearls. They are made from tapioca. Tapioca is made from the root of a plant.
Here is the surprising part. **In Taiwan, you choose how sweet your drink is. You also choose how much ice is in it.** The staff will ask you, so have your answer ready.

| Sugar level | How sweet |
|---|---|
| regular sugar | 100% |
| less sugar | 70% |
| half sugar | 50% |
| light sugar | 30% |
| no sugar | 0% |
The ice levels are **regular ice**, **less ice**, **no ice** and **hot**.

Why so many choices? **Regular sugar is very sweet, so many local people choose half sugar or light sugar.** Many also ask for less ice. Ice turns into water and makes the tea weak. With less ice, the tea is stronger.
A good first order is **pearl milk tea, half sugar, less ice**. Most cups cost NT$45 to NT$75.

images.alt: A Taiwanese breakfast shop counter with a rolled egg pancake cut into pieces, a cup of soy milk and a cup of pearl milk tea with black pearls at the bottom

blocks.title: Part 3: Taipei 101
paragraphs: In the afternoon, take the Red Line to Taipei 101/World Trade Center Station. **Taipei 101 is the tallest building in Taiwan: 508 metres high, with 101 floors.** When it opened about twenty years ago, it was the tallest building in the world.

**The observatory is on the 89th floor, about 380 metres above the street.** An observatory is a high place for looking at the view. From the windows, you see the city and the green mountains around it.

- Open: every day, 10:00 am to 9:00 pm
- Last entry: 45 minutes before closing, at 8:15 pm
- Adult ticket: NT$600
Many visitors go up just before the sun goes down. **This way, they see the city in daylight and then with all its night lights.**
Near the top of the tower, there is a very big gold ball. It is called a **damper**. **It weighs 660 tonnes and is between the 87th and 92nd floors.** Visitors can see it from the observatory.

Why does a building need a very big ball? **Taiwan has very strong storms and earthquakes.** When strong wind pushes the tower one way, the ball moves the other way. **This makes the tower move less**, so people at the top feel safe and comfortable.

images.alt: A giant gold steel ball hanging inside the top of Taipei 101, with visitors looking at it from the observatory

items.prompt: What does the big gold ball in Taipei 101 do?
items.answer: When wind pushes the tower, the ball moves the other way. So the tower moves less.

rows.example: I'd like tickets for two adults, please. We want to go to the 89th floor.

blocks.title: Part 4: Raohe Night Market
paragraphs: In the evening, take the Green Line to Songshan Station and leave by Exit 5. **Raohe Night Market is a short walk from there.** It is one long street, about 600 metres, full of food stalls. It opens at about 5 p.m. and closes at midnight, every day.

A night market is a street market that opens in the evening. **People go there for dinner: they walk, talk with friends and try many small dishes.** Each dish is small and cheap. So you can try five or six things in one night.

**The most famous food here is the black pepper bun.** It is a small round bun. It has pork, green onion and a lot of black pepper in it. The cook puts it on the wall of a very hot clay oven. It gets brown and crispy.

Each one costs about NT$65. The most famous stall is Fuzhou Shizu Black Pepper Bun. It is at the start of the market. It is in the Michelin Guide, a famous book about good food. **So people often wait in line for 20 to 30 minutes.**

Next, try **herbal pork rib soup**. The meat cooks slowly in a dark soup. The soup has herbs: plants that people also use as medicine. **Many people believe this soup makes you warm.** So it is popular on cool nights. A bowl costs about NT$100.
Ordering food here is easy:

- Point at the food and say how many.
- Say if you want to eat here or take it away.
- Pay the person at the front.
- Step to the side to eat, so other people can order.
**Most food places at the night market take only cash.** Bring small notes, like NT$100 notes. A busy stall often has little change, so a NT$1,000 note is a problem.

images.alt: A busy night market street with glowing food stalls, and a cook taking round black pepper buns out of a big clay oven

items.prompt: Why should you bring small notes to Raohe Night Market?
items.answer: Most stalls take only cash, and they often do not have change for a NT$1,000 note.

blocks.title: Scene: Buying an EasyCard
paragraphs: It is 7:30 in the morning. You are at the Airport MRT station. You go to the information desk.
Phrases to use: I'd like to top up my card with ... / How do I get to ...? / Where do I change trains for ...? / Which exit is closest to ...?
Your goal: Buy an EasyCard and top it up. Learn the way to Taipei 101 and Raohe Night Market.

turns.speaker: Staff
turns.text: Good morning. How can I help you?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Hi. I'd like to buy an EasyCard, please.

turns.speaker: Staff
turns.text: Sure. The card is NT$100. That money is only for the card. There is nothing on it for rides.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: OK. I'd like to top up my card with NT$500.

turns.speaker: Staff
turns.text: No problem. That's NT$600, please.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Can I pay by credit card?

turns.speaker: Staff
turns.text: Sorry, you can only pay cash here.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: OK. Here's NT$1,000.

turns.speaker: Staff
turns.text: Thank you. Here's your card and NT$400 change. Is this your first time in Taiwan?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Yes, it is. I'm from Japan, and I'm here on holiday.

turns.speaker: Staff
turns.text: Welcome! Where are you going first?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Taipei Main Station. How do I get there from here?

turns.speaker: Staff
turns.text: Take the express train. It takes about 35 minutes, and it's NT$160. Just touch your card at the gate.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Great. This afternoon I want to see Taipei 101. How do I get to Taipei 101 from Taipei Main Station?

turns.speaker: Staff
turns.text: Take the Red Line toward Guangci/Fengtian Temple. Get off at Taipei 101/World Trade Center. It's seven stops.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: And tonight I want to go to Raohe Night Market. Where do I change trains for Songshan Station?

turns.speaker: Staff
turns.text: From Taipei 101, take the Red Line back to Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall. Change there to the Green Line. Songshan Station is the last stop.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Which exit is closest to the night market?

turns.speaker: Staff
turns.text: Exit 5. The market is just a short walk from there.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Thank you. One more question. Can I drink my coffee on the train?

turns.speaker: Staff
turns.text: Sorry, no. You can't eat or drink past the yellow line in front of the gates. The fine is NT$1,500 to NT$7,500.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: OK. Then I'll finish it here.

turns.speaker: Staff
turns.text: Good idea. Enjoy your day in Taipei!

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Thanks very much!

blocks.title: Scene: Ordering Bubble Tea
paragraphs: It is 10:00 in the morning near Taipei Main Station. You stop at a 50 Lan bubble tea shop. Yi-ting takes your order.
Phrases to use: What do you recommend? / Could I get ...? / I'd like it with ...
Your goal: Order a bubble tea and choose your sugar level and ice level.

turns.speaker: Yi-ting
turns.text: Hi! What would you like?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Hi. It's my first time ordering bubble tea in Taiwan. What do you recommend?

turns.speaker: Yi-ting
turns.text: Pearl milk tea is our most popular drink. It's black tea with creamer and tapioca balls.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: That sounds good. Could I get a large pearl milk tea, please?

turns.speaker: Yi-ting
turns.text: Sure. What sugar level would you like?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: How sweet is regular sugar?

turns.speaker: Yi-ting
turns.text: Regular is 100%. It's very sweet. Most local people choose half sugar or light sugar.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Then I'd like it with half sugar, please.

turns.speaker: Yi-ting
turns.text: OK, half sugar, 50%. And ice? Regular ice, less ice, no ice or hot?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Less ice, please. I don't want the tea to get weak.

turns.speaker: Yi-ting
turns.text: Good choice. Do you want a bag?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: No, thanks. I want to drink it while I walk around the city.

turns.speaker: Yi-ting
turns.text: Nice! Where are you from?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I'm from Japan. I arrived this morning.

turns.speaker: Yi-ting
turns.text: Welcome to Taiwan! A large pearl milk tea is NT$60.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Here's NT$100.

turns.speaker: Yi-ting
turns.text: Thanks. Here's NT$40 change. Your tea will be ready in two minutes.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Thank you. By the way, when is the best time to go up Taipei 101?

turns.speaker: Yi-ting
turns.text: Just before the sun goes down. You see the city in daylight, and then all the night lights. You can go in until 8:15 pm

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Great tip. Thank you!

turns.speaker: Yi-ting
turns.text: Here's your tea. Have a great day!

blocks.title: Scene: At the Night Market
paragraphs: It is 7:20 in the evening at Raohe Night Market. After 20 minutes in the line for black pepper buns, you are near the front. Wei works at the stall.
Phrases to use: How long do I need to wait? / What's in it? / I'll take ... / Can I pay by card?
Your goal: Buy black pepper buns, pay, and ask about another food to try.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Excuse me, how long do I need to wait now?

turns.speaker: Wei
turns.text: About five minutes. The next buns are in the oven.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: OK. Is it always this busy?

turns.speaker: Wei
turns.text: Yes, every evening. Many people wait 20 or 30 minutes.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I waited 20 minutes! What's in them?

turns.speaker: Wei
turns.text: Pork, green onion and a lot of black pepper.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: How do you cook them?

turns.speaker: Wei
turns.text: We put them on the hot wall of that big oven.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: They look really good!

turns.speaker: Wei
turns.text: (Five minutes later, you are at the front.) Thanks for waiting! The new buns are ready, and you're next. How many would you like?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I'll take two, please.

turns.speaker: Wei
turns.text: Two. That's NT$130.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Can I pay by card?

turns.speaker: Wei
turns.text: Sorry, cash only.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: No problem. Here's NT$200.

turns.speaker: Wei
turns.text: Here's NT$70 change. Be careful, they are very hot. Where are you from?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I'm from Japan. It's my first time in Taiwan.

turns.speaker: Wei
turns.text: Welcome! What did you do today?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I went up Taipei 101 and had my first bubble tea.

turns.speaker: Wei
turns.text: A great day! After this, try the herbal pork rib soup. You can find it on this street.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: What's in it?

turns.speaker: Wei
turns.text: Pork on the bone, cooked slowly in a dark soup with herbs. People say it makes you warm.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: How much is a bowl?

turns.speaker: Wei
turns.text: About NT$100.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Thanks! I'll try it.

turns.speaker: Wei
turns.text: Enjoy the night market!

blocks.title: Speaking
paragraphs: With a partner, take turns buying Taipei 101 tickets with the real price and times.

blocks.title: Final Reflection
blocks.intro: Today you rode the MRT. You ordered breakfast and bubble tea. You went up Taipei 101 and ate at a night market.
